paper_metadata.title: Achieving an appropriate strength-ductility synergy of Nbss/Nb5Si3 in situ composites governed by gradient annealing heat treatment

evidence.quote: Nb–Si based alloys

other.cycles: at least five repetitive cycles of melting

evidence.quote: Several ingots (weight 1500 g each) with a nominal compositions of Nb-16Si-23Ti-4Cr-2Al-2Hf-0.4Re (at.%) were fabricated by vacuum non-consumable arc-melting (VCAM) in high purity protective argon (99.99 wt%) atmosphere. To guarantee homogeneity of chemical composition, at least five repetitive cycles of melting for all ingots were performed

In the liquid metal cooling (LMC) furnace, a series of DS experiments were conducted and the corresponding technological parameters such as vacuum pressure, holding temperature, withdrawal rate and distance were 5.0 × 10 3 Pa, 1980 ◦C, 500 μm/s and 195 mm respectively.

After directional solidification, all these specimens were conventional annealed (I-Stage) in high vacuum heat treatment furnace at 1450 ◦C for 12 h, the process with average rates of heating and cooling were approximately 12.5 ◦C/min 1 and 10 ◦C/min 1.
